doc.title: Ray Shiner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 1998

chapter: Marriage and freelancing in New York
title: Clark Terry and Rob McConnell with the Central New York Jazz Band
summary: Clark Terry played Syracuse and dedicated a tune to Shorty; McConnell sent an arrangement for Kristen on vibes.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: She’s a great drummer. When Clark Terry — of course my ambition when I moved to Syracuse, I said to my wife, I says, “I’m going to get Clark to play with me in Syracuse.” And it took a few years. Finally I called Clark up and I said, “I want you to play with the band.” He says, “Okay, when?” And he was very sick with diabetes. He got off the plane in a wheelchair, and we brought him to the Civic Center in Syracuse where he played with us, with the Central New York Jazz Band. And he absolutely killed the crowd. Of course he called Kristen to come up in front of the audience to sit in with us to play drums. He says, “We dedicate this one to Shorty,” that’s my wife. And of course I started to cry.
Yeah. That was a great event. You guys did a good thing there with that orchestra.

We had a good time. And the guys in the band killed me though. Krissy sat in and she starts on the hi-hat [scats]. And the guys in the band would come in, and he says, “Why can’t she play with us?” — which was not really a compliment, but she did a nice job. I wanted her to play because the concert before, Rob McConnell was our soloist, from the Boss Brass, and he had one arrangement on an old record of his that I loved, “Every Time We Say Goodbye” — I says, “Hey I want to do ‘Every Time We Say Goodbye.’” He says, “Oh that’s old stuff, we don’t do that anymore. So this was in September — November rather. And come Christmas he said — he called me up on the phone and he says, “You’ve got a package in the mail coming, look for it.” He found the score to “Every Time We Say Goodbye” and he sent it to me. Woof. So I had, Cal Custer was our pianist, and he was an ace computer man, and he took it off and copied the parts off in computer and had a vibes part, and I called Krissy up, my daughter, and I says, “You’re
playing vibes on my next concert. Anyway, I’m waxing nostalgically here, but I’ve had a wonderful time in music.
